key_insight: A transverse-field Ising model with a global, non-monotonic time-dependent field can simulate arbitrary quantum circuits with only polynomial overhead, making it polynomially equivalent to the gate model of quantum computation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a theoretical bridge between analog Ising hardware and universal quantum computation, informing the design and control requirements for quantum simulators, annealers, and global-drive platforms.
method: Builds on Cesa–Pichler global control ideas for Rydberg atoms
Constructs a circuit-simulation protocol using only a global transverse field
Proves polynomial overhead in time, qubit count, and energy scale
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a formal construction and complexity-theoretic result, rather than empirical benchmarking or hardware experiments.
watch_item: The polynomial overheads are described as large, so the approach is not currently practical for near-term hardware implementations.
paper_title: Polynomial equivalence of the global transverse-field Ising model and the gate model of quantum computation
